item.title: Konnor Griffin, Pirates chase series win against struggling Angels
item.description: It took 10 seconds for rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin to make an impact in his return to the Pittsburgh Pirates' lineup on Friday night after missing 49 games because of a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: It took 10 seconds for rookie shortstop Konnor Griffin to make an impact in his return to the Pittsburgh Pirates' lineup on Friday night after missing 49 games because of a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger. Make that 10.14 seconds, to be exact. That's how long it took Griffin to dash from first base to home in the second inning on a double down the right-field line by Jake Mangum and score the only run in a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels on Friday. "Two outs, as soon as he hit it I was thinking score, and (third base coach Tony) Beasley loves to send, and we did it. We got it done," Griffin said. "I'm not sure anybody else in the major leagues scores on that ball," Pittsburgh manager Don Kelly said. "That was unbelievable. ... That's Konnor. And the electricity that he brings overall, and what he's able to do and how he's able to change the game." It was the fifth win in the past six games for the Pirates (70-72), who remain 4 1/2 games behind the San Diego Padres in the race for the final National League wild-card playoff spot with 20 games to go. Pittsburgh will try to win its fourth consecutive series on Saturday night when it sends right-hander Braxton Ashcraft (14-5, 3.59 ERA) to the mound against Los Angeles left-hander Yusei Kikuchi (0-5, 5.65). It will be Ashcraft's first career appearance against the Angels. He is 5-1 with a 2.66 ERA over his last seven starts, including a 5-4 victory at St. Louis on Sunday, when he allowed two runs on six hits in five innings with three strikeouts. Los Angeles (53-88) has lost three straight games and 10 of its last 11. The Angels need to go at least 10-11 in their final 21 games to avoid the first 100-game loss season in franchise history. Kikuchi, an All-Star in 2025, is 1-1 with a 5.00 ERA in four career appearances (three starts) against Pittsburgh, including 1-0 with a 3.55 ERA in three appearances (two starts) at PNC Park. It will be Kikuchi's third start since he missed almost four months due to left shoulder inflammation. He took the loss in a 5-2 setback to the Philadelphia Phillies on Sunday in Anaheim, Calif., when he allowed two runs on six hits, a walk and three strikeouts in seven innings. It marked the first time since Aug. 20, 2025, against the Reds that he pitched seven innings. "I think my fastball was really good today, especially the fastball command," Kikuchi said after Sunday's game. "Being able to pitch inside, east-west, where I wanted to. I had no complaints." Both runs allowed came on solo homers, the first one in the third inning by J.T. Realmuto on a slider in the middle of the plate, and the second on a high splitter to Edmundo Sosa in the seventh. "I thought Kikuchi pitched great," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said. "I felt the location of his fastball was better. Used some breaking balls. Seven innings, two runs, and it was two solo shots, so I thought he pitched great." --Field Level Media

item.title: Perú decreta que militares y policías asuman control de penales de alta peligrosidad
item.description: Perú declaró estado de emergencia en cinco penales de alta peligrosidad para permitir que policías y militares tomen el control de esos recintos, en busca de frenar la inseguridad ciudadana, según un decreto del gobierno publicado el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Perú declaró estado de emergencia en cinco penales de alta peligrosidad para permitir que policías y militares tomen el control de esos recintos, en busca de frenar la inseguridad ciudadana, según un decreto del gobierno publicado el sábado. La emergencia, que tendrá una vigencia de 60 días, permitirá además a las fuerzas armadas y la policía ejecutar acciones para "garantizar el espacio aéreo y el espectro electromagnético inmediato de las cárceles", según el decreto del gobierno de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, quien asumió al poder a fines de julio. En un comunicado presidencial, el gobierno dijo que la medida busca combatir "a las organizaciones criminales que dirigen sus delitos desde las cárceles hacia el exterior". Los cinco penales en emergencia albergan cerca del 50% de los internos vinculados a organizaciones criminales, agregó. Perú enfrenta una ola de delincuencia con una tasa de homicidios que aumentó a 10,7 por cada 100.000 habitantes el año pasado, frente al 10,1 en el 2024, según datos oficiales. El domingo previo, un grupo de sicarios vestidos como policías asesinó a cuatro personas y secuestró a un empresario que operada una mina informal en el norte del país, y luego de unas horas fue liberado tras pagar un rescate, según la policía. El gobierno ha solicitado al Congreso poderes legislativos por 120 días para aprobar una serie de medidas contra el avance del crimen, entre ellas declarar a las organizaciones criminales como "terroristas"; además para prevenir los efectos del fenómeno climático de El Niño. La oposición en el Congreso ha mostrado reparos en el pedido de la líder derechista, que prometió en su campaña electoral mano dura contra la inseguridad como gobernó su padre, el fallecido exmandatario Alberto Fujimori, quien estuvo en prisión condenado por abusos a los derechos humanos.

item.title: Infantino asistirá al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice
item.description: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, asistirá el sábado al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice, el primer torneo organizado por el organismo rector del fútbol mundial desde que abandonara su propuesta de vender una participación en el Mundial.
item.dc:creator: Iain Axon
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, asistirá el sábado al partido inaugural del Mundial Femenino Sub-20 en Katowice, el primer torneo organizado por el organismo rector del fútbol mundial desde que abandonara su propuesta de vender una participación en el Mundial. El dirigente suizo descartó el plan —que valoraba los derechos comerciales de la Copa del Mundo y otros torneos de la FIFA en 20 000 millones de dólares— a finales de julio, ante la feroz reacción de los organismos regionales de gobierno, entre ellos la UEFA europea, y de las principales partes interesadas del deporte. Un portavoz de la Federación Polaca de Fútbol confirmó que Infantino, en medio de la polémica, estaría presente en el partido inaugural. Se espera que unas 15.000 personas asistan a los dos primeros partidos del sábado. El evento constituye un importante torneo de desarrollo para el fútbol femenino, ya que muchas de las jugadoras aspiran a participar en la Copa del Mundo femenina absoluta que se celebrará en Brasil el año que viene. Polonia se enfrentará a Argentina y México jugará contra Benín en Katowice en la jornada inaugural.

item.title: Embajador EEUU visita localidad palestina en medio de recrudecimiento de violencia de colonos en Cisjordania
item.description: El embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, Mike Huckabee , se reunió el sábado con palestinos estadounidenses, entre ellos familiares de ciudadanos estadounidenses asesinados por colonos israelíes, en una localidad palestina de la Cisjordania ocupada que ha sido objeto de ataques por parte de los colonos .
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: El embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, Mike Huckabee , se reunió el sábado con palestinos estadounidenses, entre ellos familiares de ciudadanos estadounidenses asesinados por colonos israelíes, en una localidad palestina de la Cisjordania ocupada que ha sido objeto de ataques por parte de los colonos . La visita se produce en un momento en que la violencia de los colonos —y lo que se percibe ampliamente como la inacción del Gobierno israelí— ha suscitado cada vez más condenas internacionales, incluso por parte de aliados de Estados Unidos. El Gobierno israelí ha condenado la violencia de los colonos, aunque los autores rara vez son detenidos y aún menos a menudo procesados. Washington no ha criticado al Gobierno del primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu por la violencia, aunque ha pedido que se juzgue a los autores, a quienes Huckabee ha calificado de terroristas. Huckabee calificó de constructiva su reunión en Turmus Ayya, donde la mayoría de los residentes palestinos de la localidad son ciudadanos estadounidenses. Aunque Huckabee, pastor bautista y defensor desde hace mucho tiempo de los asentamientos israelíes, ha pedido anteriormente que se juzgue a los colonos violentos, también afirma que cree que estos representan una minoría de la comunidad de colonos, que asciende a unos 750.000. Alrededor de tres millones de palestinos viven en Cisjordania, y se estima que decenas de miles de ellos son ciudadanos estadounidenses. Los palestinos de Cisjordania se han enfrentado a un recrudecimiento de la violencia de los colonos, al tiempo que sus libertades se han visto cada vez más restringidas bajo la ocupación militar desde que la coalición de Netanyahu, la más de extrema derecha de la historia de Israel, llegó al poder a finales de 2022. En Turmus Ayya, los palestinos se enfrentan a lo que el alcalde Nawwaf Zaghoul ha calificado de ataques constantes por parte de los colonos. Según él, alrededor del 80 % de los residentes de esta localidad palestina tienen la ciudadanía estadounidense. Alrededor de la localidad se han establecido asentamientos israelíes, entre ellos Shiloh, que Huckabee ha visitado en dos ocasiones desde 2025. Huckabee, el primer cristiano evangélico en ocupar el cargo de embajador de Estados Unidos en Israel, se refiere a Cisjordania como Judea y Samaria, su nombre bíblico, que utiliza el Gobierno israelí pero que no ha sido adoptado por Estados Unidos. Huckabee declaró a los periodistas en Turmus Ayya que al Gobierno israelí le interesaba tomar medidas contra quienes llevaban a cabo "conductas delictivas y actos de terrorismo", y que un "pequeño grupo de meros merodeadores", que según él ascendía a unos pocos cientos de personas, estaba dañando la reputación del país.

item.title: Croatie Manifestation à Zagreb pour réclamer le nettoyage de déchets
item.description: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes se sont rassemblées samedi sur la place centrale de Zagreb pour protester contre l'inaction du gouvernement face à l'accumulation de plus de 30.000 tonnes de déchets dans une région du centre de la Croatie.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des dizaines de milliers de personnes se sont rassemblées samedi sur la place centrale de Zagreb pour protester contre l'inaction du gouvernement face à l'accumulation de plus de 30.000 tonnes de déchets dans une région du centre de la Croatie. La manifestation, l'une des plus importantes en Croatie depuis plusieurs années, a été baptisée "Marche pour la Lika", du nom de la région montagneuse où sont stockés les déchets. Les autorités ont découvert l'an dernier entre 34.000 et 37.000 tonnes de déchets, importés d'Italie pour la plupart entre 2023 et 2024, sur un site proche de la ville de Gospic, dans la région de Lika en Croatie. Le gouvernement s'est engagé à dépolluer le site, mais les organisations environnementales dénoncent le peu de progrès réalisés. Les écologistes affirment que ces détritus, où figurent des déchets médicaux et industriels, contaminent l'air, le sol et l'eau de Lika, une région réputée pour ses vastes étendues naturelles préservées. Ils reprochent au gouvernement sa lenteur à les éliminer. Les manifestants brandissaient des banderoles sur lesquelles on pouvait lire : "Les poumons de la Croatie ne peuvent plus respirer", "Arrêtez la destruction de la Croatie" et "La nature ne pardonne pas". "Nous sommes insatisfaits de la réponse du gouvernement. Le site aurait dû être nettoyé depuis longtemps", a déclaré Verica Jurnjak, venue de Gospić pour l'occasion. "C’est une honte que personne ne se soucie de nos enfants et de leur avenir." Le Premier ministre, Andrej Plenkovic, s'est rendu à Gospic mercredi et a déclaré que le gouvernement avait désigné un entrepreneur pour la première phase de nettoyage consistant à retirer les déchets du site. L'acteur croate Rade Serbedzija, internationalement connu pour ses rôles dans des films hollywoodiens tels que "Snatch" et "Mission : Impossible II", était présent à la manifestation. "Je suis ici parce que je dois y être. C’est notre devoir de défendre notre pays", a-t-il déclaré. "Ce qui s’est passé est une honte, et quelqu’un doit en répondre."

item.title: Juan Soto, Mets strive to claim series against Rafael Devers and Giants
item.description: Juan Soto and Rafael Devers are putting up big numbers for sub-.500 teams.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Juan Soto and Rafael Devers are putting up big numbers for sub-.500 teams. Soto and the New York Mets will look to clinch another series win on Saturday afternoon, when they host Devers and the San Francisco Giants in the middle game of a three-game set. Left-hander Zac Thornton (3-4, 2.93 ERA) will start for the Mets against Giants right-hander Anthony Molina (2-0, 3.77). The Mets hit five home runs on Friday, when Nolan McLean grinded through six innings and earned the win as New York held off a late Giants rally in a 10-6 victory. Soto didn't get in on the homer-hitting fun Friday, when he finished 0-for-4 with an RBI forceout, a run and a stolen base. Francisco Alvarez delivered a pair of solo blasts while Mark Vientos (three-run homer), Bo Bichette (two-run homer) and Francisco Lindor (two-run homer) went deep with at least one runner on. But Soto's presence in the lineup after missing five weeks with a strained left calf is a reminder the Mets (64-77) haven't given up on the season despite residing in last place in the National League East for much of the summer. Soto is 4-for-21 with two homers and four RBIs in six games since his return. But his season-long OPS of .934 would rank second in the NL -- behind leading NL Most Valuable Player candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong -- if he had enough plate appearances to qualify and is just below his career mark of .947. "Anytime you are stepping on the field (in) a major league game, games are important and wins and losses are important," Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said Friday. "I think that's what Juan's presence means. That's what him battling to get back as quickly as he (did) means to us and to the group." Staying healthy hasn't been a problem this season for Devers, who has played in all 142 games while serving as one of the few bright spots for the Giants (58-84), who are on pace for just their second 90-loss season since 2009. Devers single-handedly kept the Giants in the game Friday, when he finished 3-for-4 with five RBIs. He opened the scoring for San Francisco with a two-run double in the third inning and hit a three-run homer in the eighth to pull the visitors to 9-6 and force the Mets to go to closer Kodai Senga. Alvarez hit his second homer in the bottom of the eighth, after which Senga threw a hitless ninth in a non-save situation. Devers has at least two hits in seven of his last 12 games, a stretch in which he is hitting .413 with seven homers and 18 RBIs. He has 33 homers, five shy of his career high set with the Boston Red Sox in 2021 and the most for a San Francisco slugger since all-time home run king Barry Bonds went deep 45 times in 2004. "Attitude, preparation, all those things are just spilling out on the field during the game," Giants manager Tony Vitello said. "You are seeing an exceptional player be who he is." Thornton didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he allowed two runs over five innings as the Mets fell to the Houston Astros 6-3. Molina earned the victory in his first start of the season on Monday after giving up three runs over five innings in the Giants' 7-3 win over the Atlanta Braves. Thornton has never opposed the Giants, and Molina is 0-0 with a 9.00 ERA in two career relief appearances against the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Farage and Bardella's 'small boats' pact draws criticism in France
item.description: A plan agreed by Britain's populist Reform UK party and France's National Rally, aimed at sending asylum seekers who arrive in Britain in small boats back to France, drew criticism from several French presidential election candidates on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A [USN:L6N44W0QT TEXT:"plan"] agreed by Britain's populist Reform UK party and France's National Rally, aimed at sending asylum seekers who arrive in Britain in small boats back to France, drew criticism from several French presidential election candidates on Saturday. A memorandum of understanding signed on Friday by Reform leader Nigel Farage and National Rally (RN) chief Jordan Bardella is intended to go into effect if the two parties win power. Edouard Philippe, a former prime minister who is the conservative presidential candidate for the Horizons party in the 2027 election, said the pact was a "U-turn" for RN. "Seeing Jordan Bardella sign an agreement that provides for sending back to France migrants intercepted in the Channel, that one we didn't see coming," he said, asking whether the party's presidential candidate, Marine Le Pen, was "on the same page" as Bardella. Former Prime Minister and leader of the center-right Renaissance party Gabriel Attal said the pact showed the "submission " of the National Rally to foreign interests. "We are reaching levels of unpreparedness and submission that are almost never seen in the recent history of the National Rally. This shows their foreign policy is one of great submission to other powers," Attal said. Far-left leader and presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon said on X that if the deal comes to fruition, "Our country would become the gatekeeper of the English. Not voting for Le Pen in 2027 becomes a matter of national dignity." Centre-left candidate Raphaël Glucksmann of the Place Publique party told BFM TV: "That's the hallmark of the National Rally: weakness when it comes to defending France's interests. Look at their votes in the European Parliament...We are the true patriots." Bardella dismissed the criticism. "So I welcome this agreement, and if tomorrow we are in power, and Nigel Farage is as well, we will do everything in our power to curb immigration both in France and in England," he said.

item.title: At their home away from home, Brewers pursue another win against Reds
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have made themselves at home at Great American Ball Park this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Milwaukee Brewers have made themselves at home at Great American Ball Park this season. The Brewers will look to record their fifth win in as many games in Cincinnati this season on Saturday when they play the second contest of their three-game series versus the Reds. Milwaukee is 7-1 on the season against the Reds. Milwaukee benefited from a costly error by shortstop Elly De La Cruz that helped ignite a five-run fifth inning in a 10-7 victory in the series opener on Friday. De La Cruz misplayed a possible double play, leading to bases loaded for the Brewers with no outs. Brice Turang was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded and rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch to send the Brewers (88-54) to the win against the Reds (67-74). Turang went 3-for-4 with three RBIs on Friday after going 3-for-24 with 11 strikeouts in his previous six games. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy was asked if the struggling second baseman is being adversely affected by his knee injury. "He's affected, but it all comes down (to) guys go through ups and downs every season," Murphy said. "Remember two weeks ago when we were panicked about (Christian) Yelich?" Yelich hit only .229 in August but perhaps has righted the ship since the calendar flipped to September, going 5-for-15 with one homer, two RBIs and five runs during his four-game hitting streak. Cincinnati manager Terry Francona doesn't seem as concerned about facing Yelich or Turang as he does his team's defense, namely what happened on De La Cruz's error. "I went back and looked at it a couple times," Francona said. "It went right in between (base runner William) Contreras' legs. I don't know if it snuck up on Elly after that. It was unfortunate." The loss spoiled a banner day for the Venezuela-born Eugenio Suarez, who belted a three-run homer in his return following a two-game absence due to taking the U.S. naturalization test in Miami. "It's very, very cool," Francona said of Suarez becoming a U.S. citizen. "He was excited and he should be. It's very neat." Suarez will look for a repeat performance against Milwaukee right-hander Dustin May (6-9, 4.69 ERA), who will look to record his first win in nearly one full month on Saturday. Acquired from the St. Louis Cardinals at the trade deadline, May won his first start with the Brewers on Aug. 6, 5-2 over the Pittsburgh Pirates. May fell to 0-2 in his past four starts after allowing four runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-4 setback to the Texas Rangers on Sunday. He pitched well in his lone career encounter versus Cincinnati on July 24 as a member of the Cardinals. He took a no-decision despite permitting one run on seven hits in six innings of the 4-2 loss. Reds left-hander Andrew Abbott (6-10, 4.49) will provide the opposition on Saturday. Abbott lost his third straight start last Saturday, tying season highs in runs (seven) and hits (eight) allowed in a 17-5 shellacking by the Chicago Cubs. He gave up three homers in his three innings of work. He received a no-decision in his lone appearance versus Milwaukee this season, allowing two runs on five hits -- albeit with five walks -- in five innings in a 4-2 loss. All told, Abbott is 3-4 with a 3.73 ERA in nine career appearances (all starts) against the Brewers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tens of thousands rally in Zagreb over Croatia waste cleanup delays
item.description: Tens of thousands of people gathered in Zagreb's central square on Saturday to protest the government's failure to begin cleaning up more than 30,000 tons of waste in central Croatia that environmentalists say is polluting the drinking water in the area.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people gathered in Zagreb's central square on Saturday to protest the government's failure to begin cleaning up more than 30,000 tons of waste in central Croatia that environmentalists say is polluting the drinking water in the area. The protest, one of the biggest in Croatia in several years, was dubbed "Walk for Lika", after the mountainous region where the waste is stored. Authorities last year uncovered between 34,000 and 37,000 tons of waste, much of it imported from Italy in 2023 and 2024, at a site near the town of Gospic in Croatia's Lika region. The government pledged to clean up the site, but environmental groups say little progress has been made. Environmentalists say the waste, which they say includes medical and other industrial waste, is contaminating air, soil and water in Lika, a region known for its vast areas of unspoiled nature. They accuse the government of moving too slowly to remove it. Protesters carried banners reading: "The Lungs of Croatia Can No Longer Breathe", "Stop the Destruction of Croatia" and "Nature Does Not Forgive". "We are dissatisfied with the government's response. The site should have been cleaned up a long time ago," said Verica Jurnjak, who travelled from Gospić to attend the rally. "It is a shame that no one cares about our children and their future." Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic visited Gospic on Wednesday and said the government had selected a contractor for the first phase of the cleanup, which involves removing waste from the site. Croatian actor Rade Serbedzija, internationally known for his roles in Hollywood films including "Snatch" and "Mission: Impossible II", also attended the protest. "I am here because I have to be here. It is our duty to stand up for our country," he said. "What has happened is a disgrace, and someone must be held accountable."

item.title: Slugging White Sox hope to capitalize on comforts of home again vs. Twins
item.description: The Chicago White Sox often turn a pitcher's mistake into deep home runs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago White Sox often turn a pitcher's mistake into deep home runs. The White Sox (74-67) will try to keep their power surge going when they host the Minnesota Twins (67-74) on Saturday night. The White Sox are coming off a 4-1 win in Friday night's series opener, in which they hit three home runs. Colson Montgomery belted a two-run shot to right-center field, and Braden Montgomery and Miguel Vargas each ripped solo shots to the same part of the park. Twins manager Derek Shelton knows his pitchers have their hands full this weekend. "They're leading the American League in runs scored," Shelton said about the White Sox. "And in this ballpark (Rate Field), if you get the ball in the air, (it's trouble). ... They do a really good job of capitalizing on mistakes, and they've done it all year long." Colson Montgomery and Vargas each hit his 30th home run of the season on Friday. Chicago holds a 2 1/2-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians for first place in the American League Central with 21 games to go. The White Sox are looking to capitalize on their ability to win at home, where they are 42-27 this season. Only the Tampa Bay Rays (47-25) have more home wins in the AL. White Sox general manager Chris Getz praised manager Will Venable for the job he has done with a young team this season. Getz also praised Munetaka Murakami, who has 29 homers and 59 RBIs in his first year in the majors. Getz expressed a willingness to seek a contract extension with Murakami, a 26-year-old who starred in Japan before coming to play in the majors. "He's been a part of the success that we've had this year," Getz said Friday. "It's helped us win games. It's helped others gain confidence up here and believe that you can win games. That's certainly something that we're grateful for and thankful that we've gotten the opportunity to get to know him further. "He's a tremendous teammate, hard worker, and he's been productive." Twins right-hander Taj Bradley (10-6, 3.85 ERA) will try to silence Murakami and his fellow White Sox hitters on Saturday. Bradley leads Minnesota with 178 strikeouts in 154 1/3 innings and is the only pitcher on the staff with double-digit wins. In his most recent outing, he earned the victory on Monday after limiting the Detroit Tigers to one run on four hits in seven innings. He walked three and struck out nine in an 11-1 win. Bradley has faced the White Sox four times in his career, with turbulent results. He is 0-2 with a 10.47 ERA and has allowed 19 runs on 28 hits and 10 walks in 16 1/3 innings. Five walks came on June 3 in an 8-0 loss as Bradley allowed four runs on seven hits over 4 2/3 innings. He struck out five. Chicago will counter with left-hander Anthony Kay (9-7, 4.28 ERA). He is winless in his past four starts and is looking for his first victory since an Aug. 8 triumph over Cleveland. In one career start against Minnesota, Kay is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA. In a 3-1 home win on May 25, he held the Twins to one run on five hits and a walk in six innings. He struck out five. Shelton acknowledged that time is running out for the Twins to make a push for a wild-card playoff spot. With 21 games to go, the Twins stand 4 1/2 games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. "It's challenging," Shelton said after Friday's loss. "(If) this game happens in May, you're like, 'Hey, we got pitched to a little bit.' But as the calendar gets shorter, it's even more challenging." --Field Level Media

item.title: Tensions simmering ahead of Orioles' rematch with Red Sox
item.description: Late-season intensity has been on display in the first two games of Boston's series against the host Baltimore Orioles.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Late-season intensity has been on display in the first two games of Boston's series against the host Baltimore Orioles. That could be part of the backdrop as the Red Sox go for their third consecutive victory when the teams meet Saturday night. Boston won its second one-run game in a row with a 1-0 decision Friday night - and by the end there were signs of tempers flaring. Tensions were brewing after a confrontation between Baltimore's Blaze Alexander, who was a base runner, and Boston second baseman Nick Sogard. This came after Alexander slid into the base as the Red Sox pulled off an eighth-inning double play. "It's a competitive game," Sogard said. "He slid in pretty hard. I didn't have a problem with his slide, but we turned the double play. I was just looking back to see how far he went. I don't know if he liked me looking back. But that was pretty much it." Alexander said he didn't want to make a big deal of the incident. "I don't know why they're upset," Alexander said. "I didn't touch him. There was more contact on the play (Thursday) night. And that's it." The Red Sox (77-65) have won two games in a row as they try to show more signs of getting out of a rut. Yet they've won only four of their last 10 games. The Orioles (69-73) have dropped the first two games of the homestand to extend their overall losing streak to four games. "It's always disappointing to lose four in a row, especially right now at this point in the season where we're at," manager Craig Albernaz said. "Yeah, it's hard, and we've done it to ourselves. We're here, and there's a game tomorrow and we still have a chance, a good chance to kind of keep this thing going." It was a missed opportunity for Baltimore given that starting pitcher Shane Baz had a strong effort Friday. A first-inning pitch that resulted in Mickey Gasper's home run proved costly. Baz worked into the seventh inning. "He knew where the bullpen was at and he felt good enough to go back out there," Albernaz said of the importance of allowing the team's relievers to mostly regroup. "It was an outstanding outing from Shane. We couldn't get anything going off of (Boston starter Ranger) Suarez." Boston starter Sonny Gray (16-4, 2.82 ERA) will attempt to add to his win total, which is tied for the top mark in the majors with Philadelphia Phillies ace Cristopher Sanchez. Gray skipped a start since last working Aug. 26 in a loss at Miami when he gave up two runs in five innings. Gray hasn't faced the Orioles this year, but he's 7-6 with a 4.37 ERA in 15 all-time starts against Baltimore. The Orioles will turn to right-hander Chris Bassitt (6-4, 4.97 ERA) as their starting pitcher. He is in search of a victory in his third consecutive start after besting both the St. Louis Cardinals and the Athletics. Largely because of time off with an injury, Bassitt has pitched in only one home game since late May. His only June appearance resulted in a loss at Boston, where he allowed three runs in three innings. For his career, he's 2-4 with 3.88 ERA in 10 starts versus the Red Sox. --Field Level Media

item.title: India's TCS unit to invest up to $7.4 billion in AI data center campus
item.description: A subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services and its partners will invest up to 700 billion rupees ($7.41 billion) to build a 1 gigawatt AI data center campus in the Indian state of Telangana, the company said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) and its partners will invest up to 700 billion rupees ($7.41 billion) to build a 1 gigawatt AI data center campus in the Indian state of Telangana, the company said on Saturday. TCS's subsidiary HyperVault has secured 264 acres in Hyderabad for the project, which will be developed in phases. The facility is aimed at AI companies and hyperscalers, supporting high-density GPU deployments for AI training and inference. At full buildout, HyperVault said the campus is expected to rank among India's largest AI infrastructure facilities. TCS CEO K Krithivasan said Hyderabad offered the scale, talent and ecosystem needed to serve global customers. The announcement comes days after TCS agreed to [USN:L6N44L0LD TEXT:"buy"] Porsche AG's (P911_p.DE) automotive and consulting unit MHP, as the company broadens its offerings beyond traditional IT services. ($1 = 94.4800 Indian rupees)

item.title: Greek F-4 crashes during an air show near Athens
item.description: A Greek two-seat F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed on Saturday during an air show at Tanagra airport, near Athens, a Greek Air Force official told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Greek two-seat F-4 Phantom fighter jet crashed on Saturday during an air show at Tanagra airport, near Athens, a Greek Air Force official told Reuters. Video footage from public broadcaster ERT, which first reported the crash, showed a column of black smoke rising a few hundred metres from spectators watching the air show. Two helicopters were battling the fire on the spot. The fate of the pilots was not immediately known, and it was unclear whether anyone in the crowd had been injured, the official said. "A search and rescue operation is under way," the official added. Loudspeakers at the air base were urging people to leave the area, according to ERT.

item.title: Coach Luis Enrique unconcerned by PSG's poor start to the season
item.description: Paris St Germain have not had as poor a start to a league season for 19 years, with Friday’s home loss to Monaco leaving them winless after three matches in the Ligue 1 season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain have not had as poor a start to a league season for 19 years, with Friday’s home loss to Monaco leaving them winless after three matches in the Ligue 1 season. Days before they begin the defence of their Champions League title, however, the Parisians have handed coach Luis Enrique a contract extension until 2030. “There is no reason to be concerned. I say that honestly. How many shots on target did Monaco have? Two. How many goals? Two. We’ll see at the end of the season whether things balance out,” he said after Friday’s 2-1 setback in which they were ahead at halftime but conceded twice after the break. “What I want to get across is that you shouldn’t look only at the result," Luis Enrique added. "We pressed sensationally, much better than in many matches when we did not concede a goal. But luck was not on our side. “Monaco know that if they play against us like this 10 times, we win eight, there’d be one draw and we’d lose once. This was that one defeat,” Luis Enrique insisted as PSG look ahead to hosting Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday in their first Champions League group game, chasing a third successive European title. Two points from three matches is their worst start since the 2007-08 season, when PSG came close to relegation, finishing 16th. In that campaign, Paul Le Guen’s side had to wait until their sixth league game to record a victory and ended up only three points above the relegation places. This time round, the Parisians are already seven points off the pace. “It is incredible motivation for my players, for the team and for the club. If you want to bet on who will be champions at the end of the season, we can place a bet. Seven points? OK, we will try to make up that deficit as quickly as possible,” the coach added.

item.title: Guardians eager to maintain dominance over Tigers
item.description: The Cleveland Guardians all but ended the postseason dreams of the visiting Detroit Tigers with two walk-off, comeback wins in their Friday split doubleheader.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Cleveland Guardians all but ended the postseason dreams of the visiting Detroit Tigers with two walk-off, comeback wins in their Friday split doubleheader. Cleveland's Parker Messick (11-8, 2.46 ERA) will oppose fellow left-hander Framber Valdez (8-10, 4.36) of Detroit in the third contest of the teams' weekend series on Saturday night. The Guardians are 9-2 this season against the Tigers, winning 14 of 17 regular-season matchups over their American League Central rival since last Sept. 16. "I'm kind of at a loss for words," Detroit manager A.J. Hinch said. "That's a good team across the way, and they came up with some really big swings in both games. But it stings a lot, all the things that are piling up on us right now." The Guardians (72-70) maintained their tenuous hold on the third and final AL wild-card position with wins of 7-6 and 4-3 (10 innings) on Friday. They increased their lead over the Toronto Blue Jays to one game and are two games ahead of the Texas Rangers. Had the Tigers (64-77) not blown a five-run lead in the opener and a three-run advantage in the nightcap, they would have closed within 3 1/2 games of Cleveland. Instead, Detroit is 7 1/2 behind with 21 games to play. "This whole day, two walk-off wins, was just a huge mood boost for all of us," said Guardians reliever Hunter Gaddis, who picked up the victory in the second game by retiring all six hitters he faced. "Not just winning but coming back in big ways with everyone contributing." Cleveland trails the first-place Chicago White Sox by only 2 1/2 games in the AL Central. Brayan Rocchio was the hero for the Guardians in the first game of Friday's doubleheader, becoming the sixth player in MLB history with a grand slam and a walk-off homer in the same contest. The Guardians won by scoring six unanswered runs. Rookie Travis Bazzana did the honors in the second game by ripping a tying, two-run homer in the eighth inning before singling off Kenley Jansen to score Rocchio in the 10th for the one-run triumph. "It's been amazing, especially today, since I came here," said Guardians pitcher Foster Griffin, who was acquired at the trade deadline from the Washington Nationals last month. "This clubhouse is full of guys who have done this before." Messick, a top contender for the AL Rookie of the Year Award, is 0-2 with a 4.60 ERA and five homers allowed over 15 2/3 innings in three career starts against Detroit. He has a 1.80 ERA in 10 starts since the beginning of July but has gone only 4-3 because of Cleveland's erratic offense. The emotional Valdez is going in the opposite direction with three losses in his last four outings, failing to reach the seventh inning in any of them while giving up 14 earned runs in 23 1/3 total innings. He is 5-2 with a 3.43 ERA in seven career games against Cleveland but has lost both starts to the franchise this season while allowing eight runs. "I'm still new to all of this, but I think everyone in here has a sick feeling in their stomach," Detroit third baseman Kevin McGonigle said. "The only thing we can do is use it as fuel and come out the next day and play harder." --Field Level Media
